_comment: The dispatch contract: ONE answer key, four frameworks.
Feature 6 step 4. The plan originally wanted a shared fixture of STAGE NAMES,
following the Frond expression corpus. Enumerating the four proved that cannot
work: the canonical ten stages described NONE of them, and the four do not
describe each other. Node streams and wraps write/end early where Ruby and
Python strip late; PHP has no WebSocket stage because its routes carry that;
only Python has rate limiting in dispatch. A fixture of names would freeze one
framework's shape and call the other three broken.
What IS shared is the ORDERING and the OUTCOMES - and every entry below was
decided by an ADR and is already covered by a real test in all four. This file
is the index of that contract, so a fifth framework, or a rewrite of any of
these four, has one place to conform to.
Each invariant names the suite that proves it. Those suites carry IDENTICAL
case names across the four, which is what makes them comparable line by line.

invariants.rule: A registered route always wins over a file at the same path. Static resolution happens AFTER route matching, never before.
invariants.why: A file can arrive from a build step, an upload directory or a careless deploy. It must never silently shadow a reviewed route.
cases: a route wins over a file at the same path
a file is still served when no route matches
an api path needs no special case now that routes win

invariants.rule: A HEAD response carries no content on EVERY path - routed, static, template, 404, 405, 500 - and still reports the Content-Length the equivalent GET would have sent.
invariants.why: RFC 9110 s9.3.7 MUST, plus its SHOULD on matching headers. HEAD is what link checkers and monitoring probes use to AVOID transferring a body; returning one makes every check cost a full download.
invariants.mechanism_is_per_runtime: Node wraps write/end early because it streams and has no single exit. Ruby, Python and PHP strip late at their single return. The CONTRACT is the outcome, not the mechanism.
cases: a head on a static asset carries no body
a head on a routed response carries no body
a head on a 404 carries no body
a head still reports the content length the get would have sent
a get on a static asset still returns the body

invariants.rule: pre-match globals -> match -> post-match globals -> auth gate -> route middleware -> handler.
invariants.why: The globals run BEFORE the gate so a rate limiter can throttle a brute-force login and an access log records the 401. The route's own middleware runs AFTER it, so middleware on a secured route never processes an unauthenticated request. Django, Laravel, Rails and ASP.NET all order it this way.
cases: pre match middleware runs on a path with no route at all
pre match middleware output survives a 401
pre match middleware does not open a secured route
post match middleware does not run when no route matched

invariants.rule: The after pass runs over EVERY global middleware, both phases, not just the post-match group.
invariants.why: The response phase must cover everything the request phase entered. Running only the post-match group leaked one slot per request from any acquire/release pair, unbounded, and inverted: the hook fired on the error path and not the happy one.
cases: a global after hook runs on a matched route
a pre match middlewares after hook also runs
an acquire release pair stays balanced
a global after hook does not run on an unmatched path

invariants.rule: Every successful OPTIONS response carries Allow, derived from the router's real method set - including a CORS preflight. Allow and Access-Control-Allow-Methods are different values on purpose.
invariants.why: RFC 9110 s9.3.7 SHOULD. Allow is what the RESOURCE supports; ACAM is what the CORS POLICY permits cross-origin. A policy naming DELETE on a GET-only route is still a 405, so a client reading only ACAM is misled.
cases: a bare options carries allow
a cors preflight also carries allow
a real preflight is still answered by cors
allow describes the resource not the policy

invariants.rule: A known path with an unsupported method is 405 with Allow, not 404. An unknown path is 404. OPTIONS on a known path is 204 with Allow.
invariants.why: RFC 9110 s15.5.6 + s10.2.1. Answering 404 for a wrong-method request hides the resource's existence from a client that could have corrected itself.
cases: dispatch known path wrong method returns 405 with allow
dispatch options on known path returns 204 with allow
dispatch unknown path returns 404

invariants.rule: The matched route's metadata is on the request BEFORE the auth gate and before post-match middleware, so a route marked noAuth/@noauth is honoured.
invariants.why: PHP shipped this bypass as DEAD CODE once: the metadata was assigned after the check, so a @noauth POST guarded by CSRF was wrongly blocked with 403.
cases: dispatch noauth write route is not blocked by csrf

invariants.rule: Each framework declares its dispatch stages as an ordered DATA structure, and a contract suite proves the declaration matches what dispatch really runs. Ordering lives in those lists - no stage calls another stage.
invariants.why: Every invariant above is an ORDERING claim, and an ordering that lives only in the reading order of one long function is not checkable and regrows the moment someone inlines a step. This is the structural invariant the other seven rest on: it is what makes the four pipelines comparable line by line, and what turns 'the extraction happened' into 'the extraction holds'.
invariants.structural_not_behavioural: Unlike the others, this describes how the code is ORGANISED rather than what a request does, so it is proved by a contract suite reading the source rather than by driving a request.
invariants.mechanism_is_per_runtime: Ruby uses module-level symbol arrays, PHP class constants, Node exported const arrays, Python module tuples of the functions themselves. Two checks are legitimately per-language and are therefore NOT shared cases: privacy (PHP asserts ReflectionMethod::isPrivate, Python a leading underscore, Ruby module scope, Node absence from the package index - Node has no private functions) and the arity check (Node pins only the prologue, whose stages take the raw request/response).
cases: the pipeline declares its stages in order
has no unnamed stage
a stage does not reach into another stage
